_note: video-1 music bed plan (v4 pass). Library-first: no music generated. Assembled by tools/make_stems.py --music into a STANDALONE stem (no ducking, no voice) that starts at master 0.000 and runs the full preview length, so it drops onto the editor timeline at zero against output/preview-full.mp4.
_why_body_match: Every library bed fades in AND out at its own edges (tails fall to -45..-77 dBFS), so a naive butt-loop dips audibly every 63s. Each bed is therefore crossfade-looped across its BODY window only. The bodies also differ in level by up to 8.4 dB even though all four catalog at -20 LUFS (the catalog figure integrates their own quiet heads/tails), so each bed is matched to a common body reference before the per-section artistic gain.
_body_detection: body_in/body_out come from a SUSTAINED-level test: the 3s rolling median of the clip's 0.5s-bin RMS must sit within 3 dB of the clip's body median. A single-bin threshold is not enough - one transient inside cinematic-min's quiet intro passes it, which put body_in at 0.0 and opened every cinematic-min section on 13s of near-silence.

cinematic-min._body_rms_note: POST-compression. Raw body is -23.9 dB; the compressor + makeup=4 lifts it to -18.7, so the match gain must be computed against the compressed level or sections 3/8/10 land ~5 dB hot.

_compress: Per-bed bed-taming. cinematic-min swings 17 dB peak-to-trough over 1s windows (felt piano with space between phrases) versus 2.6-7.4 dB for the other beds, so as a continuous bed it reads as dropping out. A gentle compressor brings it in line with the others; character kept, only the troughs lifted. Measured after build, not assumed.
